n: After his sermon, Alma ordains priests and elders by the laying on of hands to lead and watch over the church in Zarahemla.
Non-members who repented were baptized and welcomed into the church — Alma’s invitation was accepted.
Members who stayed proud and would not repent were removed from church records, as Alma had warned.
In this way the church in Zarahemla was set in order again.
Mormon stresses that God’s word was freely available to all; no one was barred from attending meetings to hear it.
Members were commanded to meet often and to fast and pray mightily for those who did not know God — caring for outsiders rather than shunning them.
Alma then crosses to the east side of the river Sidon to the city of Gideon, named for the faithful teacher Nehor killed.
There Alma preaches to the church according to revelation, prophecy, and his testimony of Jesus Christ. Mormon then quotes the sermon in the next chapter.

f.w: And thus it is written. Amen.
f.g: A formal closing, marking the end of a section in Mormon’s record.
